title: add vpc control plane terraform: multi-az interface endpoints, peering, route53, security-groups
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: Add a production-ready Terraform module and installer wiring to provision the VPC-based private control plane used by Private deployments. This PR implements multi-AZ subnet provisioning, interface endpoints (AWS interface endpoints for SSM, EC2, ECR, KMS where applicable), security group defaults for control-plane traffic, cross-account VPC peering helpers, and Route53 private hosted zone peering glue so customers can resolve control-plane DNS across peered accounts.

What this PR does (high level):
- New module infra/terraform/modules/vpc-control-plane supporting: multi-az public/private subnet sets, configurable CIDR per AZ, interface endpoints list, managed security groups with sane ingress/egress rules, and optional cross-account VPC peering + Route53 peering attachment resources.
- Adds upgrade/rollback hooks and migration guidance for the private-installer so existing private deployments can adopt the new module without downtime. Hooks create new subnets and gradually move control-plane nodes, with an automated rollback path that removes newly-created resources if validation fails.
- Wire-up changes in deploy/private-installer to add example var files, helm values, and orchestration steps used by our installer to call the Terraform module during provisioning and during upgrades.
- Documentation: examples and README with variable reference and recommended defaults for production (multi-az, route53-propagation checks, tagging requirements).

Compatibility and safety notes:
- The module is backward-compatible by default: existing single-AZ configs continue to work by setting az_count=1 and matching existing subnet CIDRs. The default behavior is opt-in for peering and Route53 attachments; both require explicit flags to be enabled.
- Rolling upgrade plan is included in the README and as a terraform plan target in ci to validate zero-downtime upgrades.

Testing performed:
- terraform validate + fmt in CI (green after two iterations to fix provider pinning).
- Integration smoke tests in our infra staging account: created a new VPC, verified interface endpoints, tested cross-account peering with a mirror account, verified Route53 private hosted zone resolution across peered VPCs.
- Installer E2E in private-installer CI harness using the new example var file (multi-az small cluster) to exercise upgrade hooks and rollback scenario.

Checklist (what I ran locally / in CI):
- [x] terraform validate, fmt, and unit tests for helper scripts
- [x] integration smoke in staging account
- [x] helm lint for private-installer changes
- [x] docs updated and example var files added

Notes/Follow-ups:
- We will follow up with a separate PR to add Terraform import mappings for customers with pre-existing subnets who want to adopt the module without re-creating resources.
- There is a known limitation documented in the README: cross-account resolver rules require outbound resolver endpoint permission in the peered account; installer will surface actionable error messages if missing.

Related Linear: ENG-7342 (VPC control-plane terraform), ENG-7391 (installer upgrade hooks).

review_comments: Daniel Park: Please make subnet resource addresses deterministic across runs (we prefer using index-based names with az suffix). Also add more granular tags for billing (team, env, stack).
Priya Nair (author): Updated resource naming to use format vpc_control_plane_subnet_${var.env}_${var.azs[count.index]} and added tagging.sh helper. PTAL.
Sophie Martin: Route53 peering resource looks good but confirm resolver inbound/outbound behavior. Add an explicit validation step in the installer to test DNS resolution post-peering.
Priya Nair: Added resolver validation script and included it in installer post-provision checks. Documented required IAM for cross-account resolver endpoints.

Arjun Rao: Security groups default rules are sensible; tighten egress to the minimum set used by control-plane (SSM, ECR, KMS). Also prefer referencing endpoints by id not DNS in SG rules to avoid race conditions.
Priya Nair: SG rules updated to reference aws_vpc_endpoint.*.id where applicable and added dependency ordering to avoid race conditions. Ran integration tests again.
Sophie Martin: CI plan had transient failure due to provider plugin version — thanks for pinning. Approving once CI passes.
Daniel Park: Approved. Verified upgrade hooks in staging; rollback path exercised and worked as expected.
merge_commit_message:
Add VPC control-plane Terraform module (multi-AZ, endpoints, peering, Route53) and installer wiring

See ENG-7342, ENG-7391 for context.
release_notes:
- Add new terraform module for private control-plane VPC provisioning with multi-AZ subnets, interface endpoints, security groups, cross-account VPC peering and Route53 private hosted zone peering.
- Add installer upgrade/rollback hooks and example var files for migration.
- Backward-compatible defaults and docs added.
notes: This change was validated in our staging infra account. Customers with existing VPCs who want to adopt the module without resource re-creation should wait for the follow-up PR which adds import mappings to the module.
